jobs.title: Operations Lead (TS/SCI with Polygraph Clearance Required)
jobs.description:
At Fluor, we are proud to design and build projects and careers. We are committed to fostering a welcoming and collaborative work environment that encourages big-picture thinking, brings out the best in our employees, and helps us develop innovative solutions that contribute to building a better world together. If this sounds like a culture you would like to work in, you’re invited to apply for this role.
Fluor is a leading government contractor with a proven track record of delivering high‑value technical solutions around the world to U.S. government agencies such as the DOE, NNSA, the Department of Defense and the Intelligence Community.
Job Description

Must have an active (or ability to obtain) TS/SCI with CI Polygraph Clearance
Summary:
This position performs work requiring advanced knowledge and experience related to logistics, with a special
emphasis on warehouse operations and customer service. The Warehouse Lead is a working lead who
demonstrates core leadership qualities and is flexible, has excellent communication skills and is able to
adapt easily to change.
Scope:
Under the direction of the Logistics Manager, the Warehouse Operations Lead is responsible for the daily
operations related to Material Management including shipping/receiving, material handling, material
inventory and cycle counts, forklift operation, customer service, document destruction and other tasks
related to Logistics. The Warehouse Lead is responsible for providing an array of customer driven on
demand services within a secure government facility.

Principal Job Duties & Responsibilities Include but are limited to:
• Position requires the flexibility and performance of a multitude of Integrated Logistics Support functions
related to Material Management, Transportation, Shipping/Receiving, Material Handling and Warehousing
• Efficient and safe handling of all incoming and outgoing material
• Coordinates with site management/staff to implement plans and recommendations
• Prepares plans, procedures, schedules, and develops tools for warehouse operations
• Promptly and accurately maintains Government material within all designated warehouse storage areas to
ensure highest audit rating is sustained
• Ensures Contract is in compliance with Federal, Contract and Corporate requirements and is prepared for
audits and customer reviews
• Performs physical inventories of Government material and prepare inventory and financial reports
• Creates and maintains local work instructions and procedures in accordance with applicable directives
• Monitors Material Management and Logistics processes and continuously drive process improvements
• Understands customer requirements, provides technical guidance, direction and training to co-workers and
site personnel relating to Material Management matters
• Supports movement of Government material by operating light duty vehicles and forklifts
• Supports Special Project assignments from Management or Customer, as required
• Performs other duties as directed by the Site Logistics Manager

#Intel

Basic Job Requirements

• A combination of education and directly related experience equal to three (3) years; some locations may
have additional or different qualifications in order to comply with local requirements
• Ability to communicate effectively with audiences that include but are not limited to management,
coworkers, clients, vendors, contractors, and visitors
• Demonstrate strong commitment to safety, quality, and continuous process improvement
• Job related technical knowledge necessary to complete the job
• Ability to attend to detail and work in a time-conscious and time-effective manner
• Ability to obtain and maintain forklift operator certification
• Reach with hands and arms, extending arms forward and above the head
• Climb ladders and stairs, and perform work at heights
• Lift and carry 35 pounds of material

Other Job Requirements

• Must have active (or ability to obtain and maintain) TS/SCI with CI Polygraph clearance
• U.S. citizen
Physical Demands: Performance of work may require sorting and movement of items up to 35 pounds and
may require extended walking and standing. Performs light to moderate lifting when moving material by
hand or hand-truck. May be required to operate a variety of forklifts to move, load and unload material.
Position requires the basic skills and physical ability necessary to perform assigned job functions. Employee
is required to stand, walk, sit, squat, stoop, bend, climb, lift and pull. Employee is required to use hands
and fingers to finger, handle, feel and grip material and tools. Employee is required to reach with hands and
arms, extending arms forward and above the head.

Work Environment: Generally favorable indoor office workspace and/or limited exposure to adverse
weather conditions. Will be required to use personal protective equipment such as gloves, safety shoes,
protective eyewear, safety vest, hardhat, and/or ear protection.

Preferred Qualifications

• High School Diploma or equivalent appropriate General Certificates of Secondary Education or global
equivalent, however four (4) year accredited degree or global equivalent preferred
• Ability to communicate fluently in English (read, write, and speak)
• Experience should be primarily in the area of Logistics/Warehousing
• Ability to lead a team and motivate others to be successful
• Good interpersonal and communication skills
• Good computer skills to include the use of Microsoft Office Applications

jobs.title: Sales Manager
jobs.description:
At Fluor, we are proud to design and build projects and careers. We are committed to fostering a welcoming and collaborative work environment that encourages big-picture thinking, brings out the best in our employees, and helps us develop innovative solutions that contribute to building a better world together. If this sounds like a culture you would like to work in, you’re invited to apply for this role.
Job Description

At Fluor, we are committed to building a better world by delivering innovative engineering, procurement, construction, and project management solutions.
The Sales Manager is responsible for driving business growth, developing strategic client relationships, and securing new project opportunities across targeted industry sectors within the Europe, Middle East and Africa region (EAME).
This position serves as a strategic, client-facing leadership role focused on identifying opportunities, positioning Fluor's capabilities, developing account strategies, and generating sustainable revenue growth. The Sales Manager will work closely with business line leaders, operations teams, technical experts, and proposal teams to expand Fluor's market presence and achieve business development objectives. The Sales Manager is also expected to have a strong technical understanding of the mining sector, in order to facilitate and contribute effectively in discussions with client technical teams.
Principal Job Duties & Responsibilities

•    Develop and execute strategic sales and business development plans to achieve revenue, profitability, and growth objectives.
•    Identify, qualify, and pursue new business opportunities aligned with Fluor's strategic priorities.
•    Build and maintain long-term relationships with key clients, industry stakeholders, partners, and decision-makers.
•    Develop and manage strategic account plans for existing and prospective clients.
•    Lead customer engagement activities, including executive meetings, presentations, workshops, networking events, and industry conferences.
•    Coordinate capture planning activities and develop win strategies for major pursuits.
•    Collaborate with technical, operational, and commercial teams to develop compelling client value propositions.
•    Support and drive proposal development, commercial negotiations, contract discussions, and project handover activities.
•    Maintain an active and accurate sales pipeline, forecasts, and opportunity tracking information.
•    Monitor market conditions, competitor activities, industry trends, and investment opportunities.
•    Drive customer satisfaction and strengthen long-term client relationships to promote repeat business.
•    Promote Fluor's capabilities and solutions while ensuring compliance with company policies, ethics, and governance standards.
•    Provide regular business development reports, market intelligence, and strategic recommendations to leadership teams.
•    Participate in annual business planning and contribute to regional growth strategies.

Basic Job Requirements

•    Bachelor’s degree in engineering,
•    Minimum 10 to 15 years of progressive experience in sales, business development, account management.
•    Proven track record of securing and growing large, complex business opportunities and strategic accounts.
•    Strong understanding of the mining industry, especially centered around engineering, construction and consulting.
•    Demonstrated ability to build relationships with executive-level stakeholders and key decision-makers.
•    Experience managing complex sales cycles from opportunity identification through contract award.
•    Strong commercial acumen and understanding of contract structures, risk management, and commercial negotiations.
•    Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
•    Strong analytical, strategic planning, and problem-solving capabilities.
•    Ability to work effectively in a matrixed, multicultural, and geographically dispersed environment.
•    Willingness and ability to travel within South Africa and internationally as required.

Preferred Qualifications

•    Bachelor’s degree in mining technical related field (Metallurgy, Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Structural, Instrumentation)
•    Good understanding of the design of mining process plants and the relevant technical interdependencies
•    Experience within a global engineering, consulting, EPC/EPCM, construction, technology, or professional services organization.
•    Established network of industry contacts within the target region (EAME).
•    Demonstrated success managing strategic accounts and securing large-scale projects.
•    Experience leading complex pursuits involving multiple stakeholders and cross-functional teams.
•    Strong understanding of market analysis, client engagement strategies, and business growth planning.
•    Knowledge of sustainability, digital transformation, and emerging industry trends.
•    Professional memberships with relevant industry associations.
•    Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive strategic business outcomes.

To be Considered Candidates:  Must be authorized to work in the country where the position is located.

All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other criteria protected by governing law.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Global Compensation for Strategic Projects and Project Management
jobs.description:
At Fluor, we are proud to design and build projects and careers. We are committed to fostering a welcoming and collaborative work environment that encourages big-picture thinking, brings out the best in our employees, and helps us develop innovative solutions that contribute to building a better world together. If this sounds like a culture you would like to work in, you’re invited to apply for this role.
Job Description

Summary
The Senior Compensation & Project Manager is a hybrid role responsible for strategic, enterprise-wide projects (designing, modeling, and scaling global compensation programs across all business segments globally), as well as coordinating the project management needs for the Global Compensation Team. This role requires a balance of analytical compensation expertise and rigorous project management. You will serve as the strategic engine driving the end-to-end execution of pay program redesigns, compensation cycle improvement initiatives and other key deliverables. The position combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, requiring expertise in compensation operations, analytics, and program management.

A core success component to this role is owning high-priority projects and programs end to end. You'll work closely with your Global Compensation and Executive Compensation teammates, as well as HRBPs, HRIS and other internal stakeholders, building expertise in how these programs work and what it takes to land them well.  You will identify dependencies early, proactively surface and mitigate risks, and keep complex, multi-stakeholder work moving toward clear outcomes. This is a high-level individual contributor role for someone who brings both rigor and judgment to every project they own.

Basic Job Requirements

Principal Job Duties & Responsibilities
- Leads and performs assigned enterprise-wide projects which span across business segments and geographies (such projects may include pay program redesign efforts, process improvement initiatives, support of compensation strategy development and analysis, etc.).
- Supports Global Compensation Team with project management techniques to drive improved execution across a portfolio of initiatives, ensuring that the organization is coordinated and on track to meet delivery of key solutions for the business.
- Administers the Project Status Tracker and develops reporting for senior leadership.
- Owns and delivers on various value-added projects as assigned.
- Develops dashboards which provide insights into talent management trends, pay competitiveness, labor market staffing dynamics, etc. to meet business needs and people-related objectives.
- Performs benchmarking and analysis to provide organizational compensation-related insights and recommendations for future actions.
- Participates in the Year-End Compensation Planning Cycle, both from an execution and process improvement standpoint.
- Works with the Global Compensation Team to drive towards best practices and consistent approaches and formats for supporting the various business segment customers.

Working Conditions
Indoor office workspace at the Irving, Texas headquarters.

Other Job Requirements

Preferred Qualifications

- 8 years of progressive experience in compensation, including program design and business partnering
- At least 3 years driving multi-stakeholder, cross-functional programs end to end, exercising strong project management skills (ideally at a scaling or global company)
- A track record of building from scratch: you've created processes, playbooks, or program infrastructure where none existed before, not just improved what was already in place
- Excellent written communication: you can produce an executive update, a stakeholder decision memo, and a practitioner playbook with equal fluency
- Strong foundation in global compensation programs, including multiple pay components (base pay and incentives)
- Proven ability to communicate complex compensation topics clearly and confidently to senior leadership, influencing decisions through data-driven insights
- Advanced Excel and analytical modeling skills to drive timely and high-quality delivery of insights
- Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect compensation strategy to Fluor’s business model and broader organizational goals
- Experience leading global compensation processes (e.g., annual cycles) across multiple stakeholder groups with a global mindset
- Advanced analytical skills, including compensation benchmarking, modeling, and insights generation
- Experience with SuccessFactors or similar HRIS/compensation platforms
- Track record of implementing compensation systems or tools and leading associated change management efforts, including process redesign and stakeholder enablement
- Demonstrated ability to handle confidential information with total discretion
- Self-starter with track record of proactively identifying and solving complex challenges

jobs.title: Procurement Lead
jobs.description:
Fluor is one of Canada's top employers and is recognized globally as a leader in the Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Fabrication, and Maintenance industry. Our focus on innovation and providing cost-effective technology-based solutions is second to none. As we look to the future, we need creative, ambitious, and innovative professionals who can help us fulfill our purpose to Build a Better World.
Fluor team members are at the heart of our success in executing projects safely, thoughtfully, and with the highest quality. If you value teamwork, empowerment in your career, and are eager to champion innovative and sustainable solutions to our clients, this opportunity just may be for you!
Job Description

Project Purchasing Manager is a key member of the Supply Chain team, responsible for executing procurement activities for materials and equipment in support of complex projects from pre-award through closeout.

Principal Job Duties & Responsibilities
- Execute purchasing activities and strategy development for critical engineered equipment and major bulk materials in accordance with project requirements and material management plans

- Review the project scope of work and prime contract and develop modifications to standard templates and terms and conditions for final legal review
- Prepare bid packages, manage bidder communications and clarification meetings and administer quotation timelines
- Conduct commercial bid evaluations evaluating pricing, terms, delivery, compliance and risk against project baseline documents
- Issue purchase orders and manage them through the full lifecycle, including change orders, price adjustments and supplier exceptions
- Effectively negotiate and recommend resolution to terms and conditions exceptions
- Negotiate and resolve any claims related items regarding material
- Analyze and make independent recommendations regarding solutions to problems with varying complexity in accordance with organization and/or project objectives and guidelines
- Validate supplier invoices and resolve discrepancies in a timely manner
- Provide guidance and support to intermediate and junior buyers on the project team
- Collaborate closely with Engineering, Construction, Logistics, and other project stakeholders
- Lead weekly purchasing meetings to align expectations and schedules
- Plan and organize own work assignments, as well as carry out tasks from management staff
- Organize and prioritize a variety of projects and multiple tasks in an effective and timely manner, set priorities, and meet deadlines
- Adhere to and support Fluor’s Health, Safety & Environmental and Sustainability Policies

- Meet expectations on attendance and punctuality

Job Description

In this site-based role, you will be located full-time at our project site in Kitimat, BC. Working in a fast-paced, schedule-driven environment, you will be expected to demonstrate resilience, adaptability, and sound judgment while supporting project objectives. The emphasis of the role is on employee relations, client interaction, workforce development, and people management. This position provides administrative, human resources, and employee support services across all departments and personnel on a large industrial construction project.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead and coordinate day-to-day Human Resources activities ensuring compliance with company policies, employment legislation, and project requirements.
- Serve as a trusted advisor to project leadership by providing guidance on employee relations, performance management, workforce planning, staffing, investigations, and other personnel matters in a multi-employer environment.
- Support the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, workforce mobilization, orientation, transfers, extensions, terminations, and employee engagement initiatives, while partnering with hiring managers, Talent Acquisition, and project stakeholders.
- Develop and maintain strong working relationships with project teams, clients, community stakeholders, and local Indigenous communities to support workforce development, recruitment, and employment initiatives.
- Coordinate and monitor staffing plans, personnel authorizations, workforce forecasts, organizational data, and project reporting to ensure workforce requirements align with project schedules and budgets.
- Support employee communications, training, and engagement programs while contributing to a positive, inclusive, and safety-focused workplace culture.
- Manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced project environment, providing administrative and HR support to project personnel and leadership as required.
- Other duties as assigned

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Human Resources or related field. CHRP designation or working towards the designation preferred.
- Accredited four (4) year degree or global equivalent in applicable field of study and seven (7) years of work-related experience or a combination of education and directly related experience equal to eleven (11) years if non-degreed; some locations may have additional or different qualifications in order to comply with local requirements
- Minimum five (5) to seven (7) years of progressive human resources experience with practical hands-on application of key HR competencies
- Construction or project site experience is required
- Three (3) to five (5) years of demonstrated complex employee-relations investigations experience is required
- Ability to work in a diverse, fast-paced and dynamic environment
- Able to demonstrate organizational skills with the ability to prioritize effectively and manage multiple tasks in an environment with competing demands and deadlines
- Excellent understanding and application of Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) including excel reporting capabilities; and previous experience using SharePoint is a plus.

Other Job Requirements

Preferred Qualifications

- Understand main Human Resource concepts, policies, and administrative procedures
- Good knowledge of Human Resource policies and procedures
- Demonstrated problem-solving skills of a complex nature
- Demonstrated ability to be discreet with confidential company and employee information
- Experience providing consultation to managers and HR staff
- Excellent written and oral communication skills

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Global Compensation (Urban Solutions)
jobs.description:
At Fluor, we are proud to design and build projects and careers. We are committed to fostering a welcoming and collaborative work environment that encourages big-picture thinking, brings out the best in our employees, and helps us develop innovative solutions that contribute to building a better world together. If this sounds like a culture you would like to work in, you’re invited to apply for this role.
Job Description

Summary
The Senior Manager, Global Compensation is responsible for leading the design, implementation, and administration of compensation programs that attract, motivate, and retain top talent while supporting the organization's business strategy. Acting as a strategic compensation advisor to business leaders and HR Business Partners, this role provides expertise in compensation planning, pay governance, market competitiveness, and regulatory compliance.

This position serves as the lead compensation partner for the Urban Solutions business segment and owns the planning, execution, governance, and continuous improvement of key global compensation processes, including annual merit, promotion, and incentive planning activities. The role requires strong analytical capabilities, exceptional stakeholder management skills, and the ability to translate complex compensation data into actionable business recommendations. Also, this role requires rigorous project management skills to successfully drive results which impact the company.

In addition to performing the primary compensation business partnering role supporting the assigned business segment, this role also serves as the subject matter expert for US and Canadian pay practices and compliance requirements, assisting Global Compensation Team peers in their support of their assigned business segments.

Fluor’s Urban Solutions group delivers engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) services from concept to completion, focusing on industries critical to modern life, transportation, and energy transition. This business is Fluor’s flagship growth segment, combining large-scale infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, and life sciences projects with a strong focus on data-driven design, operational excellence, and strategic alignment with global megatrends.

The Urban Solutions Group includes Advanced Technologies & Life Sciences, Infrastructure, Mining & Metals, Plant & Facility Services, and our TRS Staffing Solutions subsidiary.

Basic Job Requirements

Principal Job Duties & Responsibilities
- Lead the design, implementation, and ongoing management of global compensation programs, including base salary frameworks and applicable bonus administration for the Urban Solutions assigned business segment.
- Serve as a trusted advisor to Human Resources Business Partners (HRBPs) and business leaders, providing clear, data-driven insights and recommendations to support decision-making on compensation strategies and improvement opportunities.
- Synthesize complex compensation data and present actionable insights and recommendations to senior leadership, clearly articulating trade-offs and business impact.
- Own and drive key compensation processes such as the annual Year-End Planning cycles, including planning, execution, stakeholder alignment, and communications.
- Maintain strong governance and documentation standards with respect to compensation processes, policies, etc.
- Serve as the internal team consulting resource and subject matter expert for pay practices, market competitiveness, and statutory compliance for the US and Canada (FLSA, as well as state, local and provincial jurisdictions), helping other team members as needed in their support of other business segments.
- Perform market benchmarking and impactful analysis to meet the needs of the business segment you support.
- Exercise process improvement skills to optimize core compensation activities, both business segment-related and company/ team-wide in nature.
- Own ad hoc assigned projects and drive them to successful completion

Working Conditions
Indoor office workspace at the Irving, Texas headquarters.

Other Job Requirements

Preferred Qualifications

•     Desired 8+ years of progressive experience in compensation, including program design and business partnering
•     A track record of building from scratch: you've created processes, playbooks, or program infrastructure where none existed before, not just improved what was already in place
•     Excellent written communication: you can produce an executive update, a stakeholder decision memo, and a practitioner playbook with equal fluency
•     Strong foundation in global compensation programs, including multiple pay components (base pay and incentives)
•     Proven ability to communicate complex compensation topics clearly and confidently to senior leadership, influencing decisions through data-driven insights
•     Advanced Excel and analytical modeling skills to drive timely and high-quality delivery of insights
•     Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect compensation strategy to Fluor’s business model and broader organizational goals
•     Experience leading global compensation processes (e.g., annual cycles) across multiple stakeholder groups with a global mindset
•     Advanced analytical skills, including compensation benchmarking, modeling, and insights generation
•     Experience with SuccessFactors or similar HRIS/compensation platforms
•     Track record of implementing compensation systems or tools and leading associated change management efforts, including process redesign and stakeholder enablement
•     Demonstrated ability to handle confidential information with total discretion
•     Self-starter with track record of proactively identifying and solving complex challenges

Our offerings include medical, dental and vision plans, EAP, disability coverage, life insurance, AD&D, voluntary benefit plans, 401(k) with a company match, paid time off (personal, bereavement, sick, holidays) for salaried employees, paid sick leave per state requirement for craft employees, parental leave, and training and development courses.
Market Rate Statement: The market rate for the role is typically at the mid-point of the salary range; however, variations in final salary are determined by additional factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, relevant years of experience, geographic location, internal pay equity, and prevailing market conditions for the specific role.

To be Considered Candidates: Must be authorized to work in the country where the position is located.
Salary Range: $119,500.00 - $222,500.00
